reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
name: Suzuki Angiographic Staging of Moyamoya Disease

version.label: Suzuki and Takaku (1969), stages I–VI
version.detail: Angiographic stages of progressive steno-occlusion of the terminal internal carotid arteries and the development and regression of moyamoya collaterals.

purpose: Describes the angiographic stage of moyamoya disease.
intendedPopulation: Patients with moyamoya disease or syndrome studied with catheter angiography.

options.label: Narrowing of the carotid fork
options.detail: Stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries.

options.label: Initiation of the moyamoya
options.detail: Dilated main cerebral arteries; moyamoya vessels begin to appear at the base.

options.label: Intensification of the moyamoya
options.detail: Prominent basal moyamoya vessels; anterior and middle cerebral arteries narrowed or poorly filled.

options.label: Minimisation of the moyamoya
options.detail: Moyamoya vessels decrease; posterior cerebral involvement; extracranial collaterals increase.

options.label: Reduction of the moyamoya
options.detail: Further reduction of moyamoya vessels; main intracranial arteries absent; collateral supply mainly external carotid.

options.label: Disappearance of the moyamoya
options.detail: Moyamoya vessels disappear; supply only from the external carotid (and vertebral) systems.

resultStates.label: Stage I: narrowing of the carotid fork
resultStates.summary: Stenosis of the terminal internal carotid arteries.

resultStates.label: Stage II: initiation of the moyamoya
resultStates.summary: Dilated main cerebral arteries; moyamoya vessels begin to appear at the base.

resultStates.label: Stage III: intensification of the moyamoya
resultStates.summary: Prominent basal moyamoya vessels; anterior and middle cerebral arteries narrowed or poorly filled.

resultStates.label: Stage IV: minimisation of the moyamoya
resultStates.summary: Moyamoya vessels decrease; posterior cerebral involvement; extracranial collaterals increase.

resultStates.label: Stage V: reduction of the moyamoya
resultStates.summary: Further reduction of moyamoya vessels; main intracranial arteries absent; collateral supply mainly external carotid.

resultStates.label: Stage VI: disappearance of the moyamoya
resultStates.summary: Moyamoya vessels disappear; supply only from the external carotid (and vertebral) systems.

clinicalContext.text: Describes the natural angiographic progression of moyamoya disease.

clinicalInsights.text: Stage each hemisphere separately; disease is often asymmetric.

limitations.text: Angiographic description; correlates imperfectly with symptoms or haemodynamic impairment.

limitations: Progression does not always follow the stages in order.

confounders.effect: A single stage may not describe both sides.

guideSections.what: Six angiographic stages of moyamoya disease.
guideSections.howToPerform: Review internal and external carotid and vertebral injections; assign the stage that fits each side.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with perfusion studies and symptoms.

sources.citation: Suzuki J, Takaku A. Cerebrovascular 'moyamoya' disease. Disease showing abnormal net-like vessels in base of brain. Arch Neurol. 1969;20(3):288-299.
